data.title: When people with student debt try to save for retirement, they fall behind early and never catch up
data.description:
By Beth Pinsker

If all employers matched debt payments, workers would save more than $10 billion

Paying off student loans leaves workers behind on retirement.

A new study paints a harrowing picture of what happens over time to the 401(k) retirement savings of workers who are paying off student loans: They fall behind early and never catch up.

One-fifth of workers currently carry student loans, according to a new report from the Employee Benefit Research Institute (EBRI) in a study commissioned by Candidly, a financial-technology firm specializing in student-debt issues. Workers with this debt were more likely to drop out of 401(k) plans or contribute less if they stayed enrolled.

The research comes as student debt remains a persistent burden across the U.S. population, with $1.66 trillion in outstanding loans. This issue spans all age groups, incomes and tenures of employees. Although the largest group of workers with student loans is between ages 29 and 34, there were still a significant number of workers over 50 either paying off their own debt or PLUS loans for their children. Some 8% of workers ages 64 to 69 still were carrying student debt. In terms of income, even 9% of those earning $250,000 were paying student loans.

Most of workers with student debt were contributing less than 6%, with nearly 40% contributing less than 3%. The gulf between contribution rates of those paying loans and those without debt widened with age. For younger workers ages 25 to 29, the contribution rates for those with student debt were 7.4% lower than the unindebted cohort. That percentage difference was 14.7% lower for those ages 50 to 54.

Even after paying off the debt, the effects lingered. Using data that synced government reports with credit-bureau data, EBRI was able to "follow" the same group of participants over a five-year time span and see how the effects of this slow savings start affected the groups. The news was grim: By the time the indebted workers reached their 40s, their median account balances were about 45% less than those who didn't borrow for higher education.

"It really encapsulates everything," said Craig Copeland, director of wealth research at EBRI, who wrote the report. "Over time, that's where you see where that big difference happens."

Matching student-loan repayments

Being able to quantify the lifelong impact of student debt could have an impact on how Americans think about the "return on investment" of borrowing for higher education. A college degree may lead to greater lifetime earnings in some professions, but what about the rest of the wealth picture?

"That's about earning; what's not part of that equation is wealth and accumulation," said Laurel Taylor, founder and CEO of Candidly. "It's so hard to make up for the compounding effect early in your career. Your lifetime earnings might increase with a college degree, but what do we do about this one- to 15- year gap in retirement savings?"

One solution Candidly supports is for more employers to offer matching 401(k) contributions for student-loan repayment, as allowed by the Secure 2.0 Act. With this benefit, companies are able to put matching retirement funds into a worker's account, even if the worker isn't contributing but is paying back student loans instead. About 42% of U.S. companies currently offer this benefit, according to a 2025 EBRI report.

The new EBRI study found that more than $10 billion "in potential value" could be available for student-loan borrowers if U.S. companies universally adopted such matching policies. Up to $20 billion or more could be on the table if employees also increased their contribution rates at the same time.

"As employers think about wellness and wealth, they should see that student debt affects all groups," said Taylor. "With that as a backdrop, offering matching on student loans also incentivizes workers to pay loans and helps avoid a drop of credit score and fees if they don't."

data.title: MicroVision Showcases Expanding Perception Portfolio at IAA Transportation 2026
data.description:
New Perception Platform, next-generation MOVIA S, HALO, FMCW technology, and commercial vehicle concept demonstrate MicroVision's Lidar 2.0 strategy in action

REDMOND, WA AND HANOVER, GER / ACCESS Newswire / September 15, 2026 / MicroVision, Inc. (NASDAQ:MVIS), a leader in advanced perception technologies, is showcasing the expanding breadth of its sensing and perception portfolio this week at IAA Transportation 2026, demonstrating how lidar hardware, perception software, and open sensor integration can work together to address increasingly complex applications across transportation and autonomy.

At the center of MicroVision's IAA presence is the newly introduced MicroVision Perception Platform™, a flexible, modular architecture designed to allow sensing and perception configurations to be tailored to the requirements of individual applications.

Throughout IAA, MicroVision is bringing that strategy to life through a series of technology demonstrations and reference concepts spanning passenger vehicles, commercial transportation and emerging autonomous applications.

Visitors to the MicroVision display, located in Hall 11 Booth D02, can experience:

  • The new MicroVision Perception Platform
  • The latest configuration of MOVIA™ S short-range lidar
  • HALO™ long-range lidar
  • A first look at MicroVision's much-anticipated FMCW ultra-long-range sensing technology
  • A new commercial vehicle perception concept
  • Advances in perception software and SLAM-based mapping

"IAA gives customers the opportunity to see our Lidar 2.0 strategy come together in one place," said Glen DeVos, Chief Executive Officer of MicroVision. "We're demonstrating the breadth of our portfolio, but more importantly, we're showing how those technologies can work together to solve very different perception challenges. That's the opportunity we see for MicroVision: not simply providing sensors but helping customers build the right perception solution for the application."

Next-Generation MOVIA S Takes To the Road

At IAA, MicroVision is providing attendees with a preview of the latest MOVIA S configuration alongside HALO in driving demonstrations. The demonstration showcases advancements in point-cloud quality, perception and SLAM-based mapping and highlights MicroVision's progress toward commercial availability of the next-generation MOVIA S. Production of the new MOVIA S configuration is expected to begin in October 2026.

Together, MOVIA S and HALO also demonstrate how short- and long-range sensing can provide complementary fields of view and sensing ranges as part of a configurable perception architecture.

First Look at MicroVision's Scantinel FMCW Technology

MicroVision is also providing IAA attendees with a first look at the anticipated form factor for its FMCW ultra-long-range sensing technology.

The technology provides a glimpse into MicroVision's roadmap for next-generation lidar and its potential to extend perception capabilities across commercial, industrial, automotive, and autonomous applications.

FMCW has the potential to combine ultra-long-range sensing with additional velocity information, opening new opportunities for perception systems operating in complex and dynamic environments.

"Our portfolio is being built around a simple idea: perception should adapt to the application rather than forcing the application to adapt to the sensor," said DeVos. "That means giving customers choices across sensing range, form factor, software and architecture today while building a platform that can incorporate emerging technologies as they mature."

Bringing Advanced Perception to Commercial Vehicles

IAA Transportation also provides MicroVision with an opportunity to demonstrate how its technology can address the distinct perception requirements of commercial vehicles.

A new commercial vehicle concept combines the MicroVision Perception Platform with MOVIA S and HALO sensors to illustrate how configurable, 360-degree sensing and perception could support increasingly automated commercial vehicles. Potential applications span highway trucking, autonomous freight, last-mile delivery, buses, refuse vehicles, construction equipment, mining, and logistics fleets.

Through a demonstration at the MicroVision booth, attendees can see potential functions including object and pedestrian detection, blind-zone monitoring, free-space detection, obstacle awareness, low-speed maneuvering, and autonomous operation.

The concept builds on MicroVision's growing work across real-world industrial and autonomous applications, including mining, hauling, aerial autonomy, and other environments where reliable perception is critical to safe operation.

One Portfolio. Multiple Applications.

Together, the technologies showcased at IAA demonstrate the broader evolution of MicroVision's strategy.

Through Lidar 2.0, MicroVision has assembled a portfolio spanning short-, long- and emerging ultra-long-range sensing, complemented by perception software, SLAM capabilities and an open architecture designed to incorporate additional sensor inputs.

The MicroVision Perception Platform provides a framework for bringing those capabilities together and configuring them around the needs of different applications.

"What we want customers to see when they visit us at IAA is the breadth of what MicroVision can now offer," DeVos added. "We have the sensing technologies, software and architecture to address perception challenges across a much broader range of applications. We're building a next-generation perception company."

Experience MicroVision at IAA Transportation

MicroVision executives and technical leaders will also host presentations during IAA Transportation:

Tuesday, 09/15 at 11-11:45 AM: Safety Starts at the Bumper: How Short-Range Perception Is Closing the Near-Field Gap in Commercial Vehicles

Wednesday, 09/16 at 2-2:45 PM: The Road to Safer Autonomy: How Long-Range Perception Technologies Are Transforming Commercial Vehicles

Attendees can also participate in guided booth tours demonstrating how MicroVision's individual sensing and software technologies work together as part of a broader perception architecture.

Visit MicroVision at Booth D02, located in Hall 11 at IAA Transportation 2026 in Hanover, Germany, September 15-20, 2026.

About MicroVision

MicroVision is defining the next generation of lidar-based perception solutions for industrial, security & defense, and automotive markets. As the industry moves beyond proof of concept toward value, deployment, and commercialization, MicroVision delivers integrated hardware and software solutions designed for real-world performance, automotive-grade reliability, and economic scalability. With engineering centers in the U.S. and Germany, MicroVision leads the industry in depth and breadth of its portfolio, with both short- and long-range lidar solutions, featuring solid-state sensors with varying wavelengths, advanced sensor architectures, design-to-cost engineering, and open software solutions.

For more information, visit the company's website at www.microvision.com, on Facebook at www.facebook.com/microvisioninc, and LinkedIn at https://www.linkedin.com/company/microvision/.

data.title: Amplify Platform Launches Advisor Experience Enhancements Across Risk Tolerance, Trading, and the Client Portal
data.description:
Amplify Platform Launches Advisor Experience Enhancements Across Risk Tolerance, Trading, and the Client Portal

The new release includes three platform enhancements: risk tolerance can now be recorded on exception accounts alongside the household score; rebalancing can be managed from a single location; and clients can log into the Addepar portal with a single sign-on.

Amplify Technology, LLC ("Amplify"), the AI-native RIA growth platform built on data lake architecture, today announced three new sets of platform capabilities covering risk documentation, trading, and client access. The common thread is enabling a better user experience with fewer screens and fewer clicks between an advisor or client and a finished task.

On Amplify, risk tolerance can now be recorded on an individual account alongside the household score using the same questionnaire templates and scoring advisors already use. The Account List shows every account in the household with its current status, the source of its score, the custodian, the last risk tolerance questionnaire (RTQ) date, and its portfolio and tolerance scores.

“Every book of business holds accounts that sit outside the household profile for good reason,” said Churni Bhattacharya, Chief Product Officer at Amplify. “Advisors have been left with a household score skewed by the exception, or at risk of not accounting for the exception because it was living in a silo. Neither position would be defensible in a suitability review. Adding risk tolerance at the account level ends that trade-off.”

Trading has also been consolidated in the same release. Trade Management is now the single destination for trading activity, with expanded rebalance modes, account filtering, target weights at a glance, and lower execution drift reserves on equity sales.

“A rebalance used to require a tour of the platform,” said David Hatfield, Chief Technology Officer of Amplify. “Trade Management is now the single destination for trading activity, so the path from spotting an account to submitting trades all runs in one location. The mode can also match the account rather than the account working around the mode.”

Client access follows the same principle in the third release occurring in September. Logging into the Addepar client portal used to mean a second account and a second set of credentials. Advisors can now invite clients to the client portal directly from Clarity/CRM, so the client only needs to sign in once with Amplify credentials to access their account.

“Experience is made up of a lot of small things, not always one big thing,” said Jack Martin, Chief Marketing Officer at Amplify. “We’re constantly refining the platform, and this September release reflects a number of important changes we’ve made to improve that experience. It’s also setting the stage for what’s next: a new release coming that’s designed to redefine the digital onboarding experience.”

Wealth management firms interested in learning more about Amplify's modern technology platform can visit amplifyplatform.com.

About Amplify

Amplify is an enterprise growth platform built on an AI-native data lake. It was engineered to unify data, deliver actionable insights, and automate workflows. The platform combines a customizable chassis with experienced integration consultants and a hands-on support team to provide an integrated, scalable solution for RIAs, broker-dealers/OSJs, TAMPs, and multi-family offices. Amplify is a holistic platform that provides seamless digital capabilities for client onboarding, an institutional model marketplace, true UMA trading, client lifecycle tracking, and integrated surveillance, billing, analytics, and reporting. Intuitive dashboarding for all firm stakeholders is driven through visibility funnels that provide clarity across daily business functions. Amplify’s cloud-based, multi-custodial framework makes it ideal for growth-minded wealth management enterprises. Amplify Technology, LLC delivers technology solutions to support wealth management firms and does not provide investment advisory services. Amplify is headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona. To learn more, visit amplifyplatform.com.

data.title: TigerConnect Surpasses 1 Million Care Team Members Across Nearly 6,000 Organizations
data.description:
TigerConnect Surpasses 1 Million Care Team Members Across Nearly 6,000 Organizations

43% Growth Signals Accelerating Shift Toward Enterprise Healthcare Orchestration

TigerConnect, the AI-powered healthcare orchestration platform, today announced that more than one million care team members across nearly 6,000 healthcare organizations now use the TigerConnect suite of more than nine solutions, representing 43% growth in care team members served.

The milestone comes as health systems accelerate efforts to consolidate fragmented technology and connect the people, systems and workflows that keep care moving. Rather than adding another point solution, health systems are increasingly looking for platforms that can coordinate work across teams and systems, from pre-hospital coordination and transfers through physician scheduling, critical event and alarm management, nurse call, smart rooms and patient engagement.

TigerConnect brings these capabilities together on an enterprise platform designed to orchestrate care from pre-arrival through discharge. The platform’s growing adoption is translating into measurable results for health systems. Across its customer base, organizations have reported up to a 66% reduction in emergency department length of stay, $3.2 million in annual savings from reduced length of stay, and 50% faster door-to-needle times. Additionally, TigerConnect's Enterprise Customer Net Promoter Score of 67 reflects the strong customer satisfaction driving continued platform expansion across health systems. By connecting communication, workflow automation and AI across the care journey, TigerConnect helps health systems improve patient flow, strengthen clinical outcomes and quality, and increase operational efficiency.

“TigerConnect has become essential to how we operate,” said Brinton Muller, Director of Emergency Preparedness and Incident Command at Bassett Healthcare Network. “We serve communities across more than 5,600 square miles in rural Central New York, and TigerConnect helps our teams feel like they’re all in the same building. Whether it’s supporting emergency communications, on-call coordination or everyday collaboration, TigerConnect has transformed how we connect our people and deliver care. There’s truly been a life before TigerConnect and a life after.”

The scale of TigerConnect’s enterprise footprint is also reflected in its interoperability with leading health system technology environments. Through industry-standard integrations with the solutions hospitals already rely on, TigerConnect extends the value of that investment by bringing previously siloed tools into one orchestrated flow of care. Epic’s Showroom features TigerConnect Clinical Collaboration, Smart Room and Alarm Management, underscoring the breadth of TigerConnect solutions designed to work within health systems’ existing technology ecosystems.

“Healthcare is entering a new era where the goal isn’t simply to connect people, but to orchestrate everything that needs to happen to keep care moving,” said Sean O’Neal, CEO of TigerConnect. “Surpassing one million care team members across nearly 6,000 organizations is a significant milestone and a reflection of how quickly this shift is happening. Our customers are consolidating fragmented technologies and bringing communication, workflows, systems and AI together across the enterprise. We have the team, the technology and the customer momentum to help lead this shift and deliver better care more efficiently.”

Customer momentum is also reflected in independent market validation. According to KLAS Research, TigerConnect’s Clinical Collaboration Platform has an overall performance score of 89.1, compared with a market average of 85.6. Customers rated TigerConnect 97.9% for fair and transparent charging, while 92.5% said they would buy from the company again and 90.2% cited TigerConnect as part of their long-term plans. TigerConnect also earned a partnership score of 7.9, above the 7.7 market average.

Market recognition is expanding alongside customer adoption. In 2026, Gartner recognized TigerConnect as a Representative Vendor for Resource Scheduling for Healthcare in the Gartner® Hype Cycle™ for Healthcare Providers, 2026 — the company's sixth Gartner research mention of the year, spanning categories from clinical communication and collaboration to resource scheduling.

As health systems consolidate technology and seek greater connectivity across clinical and operational workflows, TigerConnect is helping shift healthcare from disconnected point solutions toward enterprise healthcare orchestration. With more than one million care team members now relying on the platform, TigerConnect brings people, systems, workflows and AI together to keep care moving.

About TigerConnect

TigerConnect is the AI-powered healthcare orchestration platform that automates care coordination, communications, and workflows across the patient journey. Trusted by more than 1 million care team members at nearly 6,000 healthcare organizations, TigerConnect helps health systems improve patient flow, clinical quality, and operational efficiency.

TigerConnect's EHR-agnostic platform connects people, systems, and information from emergency transfer and admission through inpatient care and discharge. Its suite of solutions spans scheduling, alarm management, nurse call, operator console, smart room, patient engagement, clinical communication, transfer operations, and more. At the core of the platform is CareConduit™, TigerConnect's workflow automation foundation. CareConduit connects signals from EHRs, devices, and clinical systems to intelligently route information and helps ensure the right person takes action at the right time.

Healthcare organizations using TigerConnect achieve an average of $1.5M in annual ROI while delivering measurable clinical and operational outcomes, including reduced length of stay, faster response times, improved patient throughput, and millions of dollars in annual savings through automation and technology consolidation.

TigerConnect has been recognized as a Best in KLAS® winner for Clinical Communications, a Leader in the Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Clinical Communication and Collaboration Platforms, and a Representative Vendor for Resource Scheduling for Healthcare in Gartner's Hype Cycle for Healthcare Providers, 2026. Learn more at tigerconnect.com.

About Bassett Healthcare Network

Bassett Healthcare Network is an integrated health system that provides care and services to people living in a 5,600 square mile region across eight counties in upstate New York. The organization includes five corporately affiliated hospitals, over two dozen community-based health centers, more than 20 school-based health centers, two skilled nursing facilities, an assisted living facility, a home health agency, a research institute, and other health partners in related fields. Bassett Healthcare Network is an equal opportunity provider and employer.

data.title: CSS Unveils Revitalized Brand, Reflecting Its Evolution as a Comprehensive Senior Living Technology Partner
data.description:
CSS Unveils Revitalized Brand, Reflecting Its Evolution as a Comprehensive Senior Living Technology Partner

CSS Unveils Revitalized Brand, Reflecting Its Evolution as a Comprehensive Senior Living Technology Partner

PR Newswire

PASADENA, Calif., Sept. 15, 2026

Refreshed identity reflects CSS's continued growth and expanded commitment to delivering technology solutions for senior living communities nationwide

PASADENA, Calif., Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- CSS today unveiled a revitalized brand that reflects the company's evolution, expanded capabilities, and growing role as a comprehensive technology partner for senior living communities.

Built around the new brand promise, "Confidence. Connections. Communities.", the refreshed identity was developed by the global branding firm, BrandingBusiness, and represents the rich legacy of CSS while clarifying the future brand positioning and business focus.

For more than 15 years, CSS has built its reputation serving senior living through DIRECTV and a commitment to responsive, accountable service. Today, CSS delivers Technology Solutions for Senior Living Communities across four critical areas: DIRECTV In-Room Entertainment; Wi-Fi, Internet & Business Communications (VoIP); Managed IT & Cyber Protection; and Modern Nurse Call Solutions.

"Senior living has never been about technology for us. It's about a caregiver who has one less thing to fight with at the start of a double shift, and a resident who can find her favorite program without having to ask for help," said Dave Saenz, Co-Founder & CEO of CSS. "Every community we serve is home to real people with real routines, and the TV in that room is often their window to the world. When we take the technology headaches off the plates of caregivers and administrators, we give them back time for the people they came to care for. That is the impact we want CSS to have, one community, one caregiver, and one resident at a time."

As senior living operators navigate rising technology costs, aging infrastructure, staffing challenges and an increasingly complex mix of vendors, CSS is expanding its role as "A partner who understands your world." The company's broader capabilities give communities one accountable technology partner and one point of contact across the critical systems they depend on every day.

"This is an exciting next chapter for CSS," said Markk Gonzales, Co-Founder & President of CSS. "We've listened to our customers, continued to invest in the senior living industry, and built our company around solving more of the challenges they face every day. Our new brand reflects the company we've become and, more importantly, our commitment to where we're going together with our customers."

The refreshed brand brings CSS's expanded capabilities and long-standing service philosophy together under one vision: "Confidence & connections for senior living communities." The goal is simple: make technology easier so senior living teams can stay focused on what matters most, the people in their care.

ABOUT CSS

CSS delivers Technology Solutions for Senior Living Communities, including DIRECTV entertainment, Wi-Fi and internet, business communications (VoIP), managed IT and cybersecurity, and modern nurse call solutions. With more than 15 years of senior living experience, CSS brings critical technologies together through one accountable partner focused on simplifying operations, improving efficiency and creating better resident experiences.

data.title: Wells Fargo just cut its S&P 500 price target. Will others follow?
data.description:
By Steve Goldstein

It's one of the first major Wall Street institutions to lower its expectations for stock-market performance since the spring

Wells Fargo strategists lowered their S&P 500 target.

In what may be a first since the early days of the war between the U.S. and Iran, a Wall Street firm is lowering rather than raising its S&P 500 year-end target.

Wells Fargo on Tuesday reduced its S&P 500 target to 7,700 from 7,950, after the index SPX closed Monday just below 7,620, up 11% on the year.

So-called top-down strategist forecasts are not as extensively tracked as Wall Street price targets on individual companies.

Strategists led by Ohsung Kwon said the downgrade comes even as the firm is growing more optimistic on earnings per share - targeting $425 next year for S&P 500 companies and $460 in 2028.

That's very optimistic. In a separate note, Bank of America analysts said the top-down consensus by strategists for 2027 EPS was $392. The so-called bottom-up projection - that is, adding up all the estimates of S&P 500 companies and then weighting by market cap - is $417.

However, the Wells Fargo team said the market is "entering late innings of the cycle, arguing for multiple compression." That refers to the multiple investors assign to each dollar of earnings. While they are not worried about 2027 EPS, they expressed concerns that AI capital expenditure would slow, eating into 2028 earnings.

Wells Fargo says 2027 EPS estimates look extreme.

Wells Fargo argued that 2027 earnings will be "cyclically elevated by 42%" compared with the trendline of what S&P 500 earnings should be at this stage of the economic cycle. The gap of 42% is the highest since the 1950s, they said.

By sector, Wells Fargo is lowering tech to equal-weight from overweight while raising healthcare to overweight from equal-weight. Within tech, Wells Fargo said it prefers software to microchips.

Tech stocks XLK have jumped 28% this year, while healthcare XLV has climbed 9%.

"We see the midterms as a potential risk to tech, especially as political pushback against data centers continues to gain momentum," the firm said.

A potential Democratic sweep would be seen as a positive for healthcare, potentially setting the stage for a restoration of the enhanced Affordable Care Act subsidies, the firm added.

Earlier this week, Bank of America increased its year-end target, albeit to levels still below Wells Fargo's new target. BofA sees the index ending at 7,400 - versus 7,100 previously - as it launched a 12-month target of 7,800.

-Steve Goldstein

PR Newswire

Clean live broadcast signal, B-roll, and reporting to be available to domestic and international news organizations

Sheen on Sept. 24 at the Dome at America's Center.

The Emmy award-winning television personality, now soon-to-be "Blessed" Archbishop Sheen is the first U.S.-born bishop to reach this stage on the path toward canonization, the Catholic Church's formal recognition of sainthood.

Feeds will be available as a Live U Matrix Distribution Channel, as well as SRT and RTMP streams.

Additional b-roll from both St. Louis and Peoria, Sheen's home diocese, will be available from EWTN News for Associated Press subscribers. B-roll and a video package is available to CNN Newsource subscribers.

data.title: Bitcoin Falls Ahead of Senate Crypto Vote, Fed Decision
data.description:
By Farhan Rafid 




  Bitcoin fell Tuesday ahead of a Senate procedural vote on the Clarity Act, with investors looking to Washington for a potential catalyst after the cryptocurrency's August rally lost steam. 



  In early afternoon trading in Europe, bitcoin was trading down 2.8% at around $76,921, according to LSEG. 



  The Senate is scheduled to vote at around 2:15 p.m. ET on whether to advance the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, which aims to establish a regulatory framework for digital assets, including rules governing their issuance, trading and regulation. It needs Democratic support to secure the 60 votes required to clear the procedural hurdle. 



  The vote is the legislation's most immediate obstacle, said Andrew Melville, head of research at institutional crypto derivatives data and analytics firm Block Scholes. Even if it clears Tuesday's vote, the Senate version contains significant revisions from the legislation passed by the House and the differences would have to be reconciled before President Trump can sign it. 



  The bill's progress has been held up by disagreements over issues including consumer protection and restrictions on public officials profiting from crypto. Senate Banking Committee Democrats have continued to raise objections to the legislation's investor-protection and ethics provisions. 



   Prediction-market traders remain skeptical that the legislation will make it across the finish line this year. Polymarket puts the probability of the Clarity Act becoming law in 2026 at 19%, down from 31% Monday. Separately, traders give bitcoin a 72% chance of ending Tuesday between $76,000 and $78,000. 



  Polymarket has a data sharing partnership with Dow Jones, publisher of Dow Jones Newswires and the Wall Street Journal. 



  Bitcoin rose around 25% between Aug. 19 and Aug. 25 and climbed above $82,000 at the start of September before pulling back. Investors have recently viewed $80,000 as an opportunity to sell, said Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares. 



  Investors are also awaiting the Federal Reserve's interest-rate decision Wednesday. Analysts have pointed to both progress on crypto regulation and the Fed decision as potential catalysts for bitcoin as it struggles to regain the $80,000 level.

data.title: College Without the Debt: How National Heritage Academies Students Are Earning a $67,000 College Degree for Free
data.description:
College Without the Debt: How National Heritage Academies Students Are Earning a $67,000 College Degree for Free

College Without the Debt: How National Heritage Academies Students Are Earning a $67,000 College Degree for Free

PR Newswire

GRAND RAPIDS, Mich., Sept. 15, 2026

Early College students can earn an associate degree while still in high school, potentially saving families tens of thousands of dollars.

GRAND RAPIDS, Mich., Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- "I couldn't imagine how much money worth of free education my kids have received through this program."

For Ciara Selden-Ruffin, the mother of Grand River Preparatory High School Early College student Aamir Hollowell, the financial impact of the Early College program has been substantial. It has given Aamir the opportunity to earn an associate degree without the family taking on the tuition bill.

That kind of financial head start is critical for families worrying about how they will pay for college.

The nation's federal student loan portfolio stands at nearly $1.7 trillion, with about 44.6 million borrowers carrying federal education debt. The issue is back in the national spotlight as changes to the Saving on a Valuable Education, or SAVE, Plan ended, requiring millions of borrowers to find a new way to repay their federal student loans.

For families with children approaching college, the uncertainty underscores a different question: What if students could reduce or even avoid some college debt before graduating from high school?

National Heritage Academies® (NHA®) Early College program is helping their students do exactly that.

A $67,000 Head Start

At Grand River Prep, an NHA partner-school in Grand Rapids, Mich., students can earn college credits, career credentials, and even an associate degree through the school's Early College partnership with Davenport University.

Tuition, fees, and books are covered through the program. Based on Davenport's current published undergraduate tuition rate, the value of a two-year associate degree can total approximately $67,000.

Felicia Pope, who works with Davenport University's Early College partnerships, said the program can put students in a very different financial position when they enter adulthood.

"You can be 18, 19 years old, you have an associate degree, you have the entry-level position in the field, without any student loans," Pope said.

Students can use that degree to begin working in their chosen field or continue toward a bachelor's degree with a significant amount of college coursework already completed. "You're halfway through your degree, saved a ton of time, a ton of money," Pope said.

Nine of NHA's high schools have an Early College program. During the 2024-25 school year, 565 students earned 5,186 college credits, saving an estimated $1.12 million in college tuition.

For NHA, the opportunity is about making college more accessible while preparing students for what comes next.

Koree Woodward, NHA Director of High Schools, says Early College is a natural extension of NHA's mission to prepare students for life after graduation.

"The program makes college feel more attainable for families who may not have otherwise seen it as an accessible option," Woodward said. "It helps students develop the knowledge, habits, character, and sense of responsibility needed for lifelong learning, college success, and meaningful careers."

College With a Support System

The financial savings are only part of the Early College model.

Students gradually transition into college-level work, beginning with one college course per semester during 10th grade before increasing their coursework in their junior and senior years.

Pope calls it a "soft launch into college."

Davenport advisors work directly with students on applications, degree pathways, scheduling, and course selection. Grand River Prep advisors provide another layer of support, helping students monitor grades, manage college expectations, and stay on track.

Aamir Hollowell sees that support firsthand.

"Every week, you have a meeting with your advisor to help you stay on track," she said. "They just keep checking up on you."

Grand River Prep Early College Advisor Jayme McWain said students get the independence of college without having to navigate the experience alone.

"For them to have kind of a safety net and a support system built in is a really great feature of that program," McWain said. "It creates so much more access and skill building."

From College Credit to Career

In addition to the tuition savings, students can leave high school with college experience, career opportunities, and potentially two years of college already completed.

For some students, that head start can translate directly into a career.

Grand River Prep graduate Kennah Kalele earned an associate degree in medical assisting through Early College and is now pursuing a Bachelor of Science in Nursing at Grand Valley State University.

"I don't have to take any gen eds in the college that I'm going to, and I'm even ahead in some aspects of my nursing degree," Kalele said.

Her associate degree also helped her begin gaining professional experience. Kalele works part time as a medical transport technician while continuing her education.

For McWain, the value is clear.

"Anytime you can help someone get free college when the price is off the charts, that's a great thing," she said.

And for families like Ciara Selden-Ruffin's, it offers the opportunity for her children to start their futures with a college education rather than a tuition bill.

About National Heritage Academies:

National Heritage Academies® (NHA®) was founded in 1995 with families in mind and the belief that every child deserves an education that builds knowledge and character. Today, NHA supports 105 tuition-free, partner-schools across nine states, serving more than 65,000 K-12 students through rigorous academics and Moral Focus™ programming. NHA

data.title: DHL to Acquire Colombian Logistics Operator Open Market
data.description:
By Sarah Sloat 




  DHL agreed to buy Open Market, a logistics and transport operator active in the life sciences and consumer sectors in Colombia, in a move to strengthen its footprint in the region. 



  Financial details weren't disclosed. Open Market has a team of around 4,100 employees, DHL said Tuesday. 



  The German logistics company said the acquisition supports its goal to grow in the life sciences and healthcare logistics sectors by 2030. 



  Open Market has a network of 21 warehouses and expertise in managing complex supply chains for pharmaceuticals, medical products and personal care, DHL said.
